## Context / Problem
Upper-bound wall-clock assertions in tests are the proven CI flake class under runner contention (19d7, 5e94, edfe, 85c3). 15 sites scanned: 13 upper-bound in scope, 2 lower-bound out of scope; 11 currently unescaped. Detector prototype (regex + escapes) caught all, 0 FPs, and found one site manual scan missed (test_lock_stale_reclaim.py:127).

## Approach
DET BLOCKING code-review criterion scanning tests/** for upper-bound wall-clock asserts. Escapes: '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' line marker, or '@pytest.mark.benchmark' (existing perf-lane convention, CI-excluded via -m 'not benchmark'). Migrations (proven by experiment): tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201 -> spy config._resolve miss path (reset_config_cache seam; regression sim caught 10/10); tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 -> exactly one pending_enrichment call + zero drain/spawn. Remaining 9 sites get markers with reasons. Optional follow-on: migrate reducer benchmarks to _api.replay_events spy to restore CI coverage (currently benchmark-skipped). Seed implementation from /tmp/exp4_detector.py; proxy rule: spy the MISS-PATH function, never tomllib (warm TOML cache evades parse spies).

## Scope
- detector as DET code-review criterion (review-bot checkout) or CI lint per gate conventions
- tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201, tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 migrations
- markers on the 9 hang-guard sites

## Testing
Detector unit tests: unescaped upper-bound assert -> finding; marker/benchmark escape -> silent; lower-bound assert -> silent. Migrated tests: regression simulation goes RED (cache cleared per call / drain forced), warm path GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detector blocks new unescaped upper-bound wall-clock asserts in tests/** with a teaching message naming both escapes.
- [ ] Both migration sites assert counting proxies (miss-path spies), proven RED under regression simulation.
- [ ] All remaining in-scope sites carry reasoned markers; detector run on the tree is clean.
- [ ] Detector has unit tests covering fire, both escapes, and lower-bound exclusion.
